Hello front-counter team,
After lunch changed little, but clear signage stayed in focus. Keep the desk lanes tidy and make sure every pet owner gets the same calm, direct guidance before they head to the gate. The Companion Animal Travel Desk should keep the handoff smooth, with checklists visible and carrier labels easy to spot.

A quick note on the Vellmar flow: <<FACT F008>> We need to stay brisk with paperwork, but never rush the human part of the conversation. If a traveler looks uncertain, walk them through the steps in plain language and point out the right waiting area without making a scene. Passengers do better when we keep our tone steady and our directions simple, and that helps the whole counter line move cleanly. Please also keep an eye on carrier condition, water needs, and any comfort issues that come up while people wait.

If you see a delay building, flag it early so the senior coordinator can shift hands where needed. Use the spare signage packs, restock the pet forms, and clear any clutter from the front edge of the desk before the next wave arrives. We are getting better when we stay consistent, stay courteous, and keep each animal moving with patience and care.
